C0.quote: normative criteria for voting rules under uncertainty about individual preferences
C0.note: Studies voting rules (WMRs, majority) over two alternatives; normative/axiomatic criteria.

C1.quote: a voting rule is Č-robust if and only if there exists a nonnegative weight vector
C1.note: Characterization results are axiomatic-type; responsiveness/efficiency is welfare-like. Strategyproofness appears only in online appendix Lemma B.

C2.2.quote: The choice of individual i is represented by a decision variable
C2.2.note: Binary choice between two alternatives, -1 or 1; a binary vote, not ranking per se.

C2.3.quote: individuals are uncertain about their future preferences
C2.3.note: Preferences over alternatives; utilities in online appendix.

C2.4.quote: An individual is assumed to vote sincerely
C2.4.note: Sincerity assumed; justification is relegated to online appendix (strategyproofness of robust rules) and is not given in the main text for the main analysis. The paper does say the profile is drawn as preferences.

C3.1.quote: An individual is assumed to vote sincerely
C3.1.note: Main analysis assumes sincere voting. The online appendix redefines robustness with insincere voting possible, but shows sincere voting is weakly dominant; main analyses are non-strategic.

C3.2.quote: An individual votes sincerely being concerned with the probability

C3.3.quote: sincere voting is weakly dominant for every individual if the mechanism satisfies robustness
C3.3.note: Justification via strategyproofness of robust rules, provided in footnote/online appendix; main text also states an incentive-type motivation (expected utility equals responsiveness).

C4.1.quote: the utility from the passage of a favorable issue is one
C4.1.note: Utility 1 for favorable outcome, 0 otherwise; the input is a binary vote.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous setting' appears but not as dichotomous preferences over approval.

C5.1.quote: a voting rule is strictly efficient if and only if it is a WMR
C5.1.note: Efficiency and responsiveness (Pareto) are the criteria.

C5.2.quote: An individual is assumed to vote sincerely
C5.2.note: Responsiveness is evaluated on the submitted vote profile, which the paper states equals the preferred alternative (sincere voting).

VOT.quote_behav: An individual is assumed to vote sincerely
VOT.note: Voters vote sincerely in the main model.

ORG.note: The social planner proposes a rule but is not modelled as an acting agent with a modelled choice or objective in the formal model.

DES.note: The social planner imposes a robustness criterion, which is a normative criterion rather than an explicitly modelled optimisation; treated as not present.

claims.quote: propose it as a normative criterion for voting rules
it prevents the collective decision from systematically reflecting only minority preferences
our analysis extends the efficiency-based justification of WMRs

C9.1.note: Claims about rule choice and voters' welfare.

C9.2.quote: An individual is assumed to vote sincerely and prefer a voting rule
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions (sincere voting, utility 1/0 linking responsiveness to expected utility) are stated, with justification in the online appendix.

C10.1.note: The paper does not state a procedural-only reading; it assumes sincere voting.
